title: A time split improves the G4466 infrared colour fit, but the evidence depends on one visit and the error floor
abstract: We test whether a fixed variable spectrum can explain 21 NEOWISE visits of the dusty dimmer G4466 in 2014-2024. We fit errors in both bands, seasonal intercepts and a search over time splits. With a 0.01 mag error floor, the residual score falls from 29.857 to 6.942 and early and late relative-flux slopes are 1.942 and 0.505. None of 1999 fitted-null simulations or 200 real control residual injections gives as large an improvement. A second published reduction gives a similar result. However, deletion of the first 2014 visit reduces the improvement to 8.502. Its separate 999-draw null test gives a tail estimate of 0.135. The first visit is supported by 14 quality-passing archive exposures, but a visit-wide error remains possible. A 0.02 mag error floor also removes the rejection, with a tail estimate of 0.126. The fit does not date a physical event or measure a dust temperature. We preserve code, source hashes, numerical checks, error-model tests and external retrieval instructions. This is an analysis of published photometry with a limited exposure check, not a new survey. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-a9439cd56862; topic astronomy; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.
